cards.title: Welcome to GNPS Program 1
cards.body: Every successful nursing career begins with strong fundamentals. Before advancing to specialised clinical procedures, every nurse must develop a sound understanding of core nursing principles. This programme is aligned with national nursing education outcomes — including those set by country-specific Nursing Councils and international regulatory bodies — to ensure globally recognised standards of care. Strong foundations create confident nurses.

cards.body: Throughout GNPS Program 1, you will strengthen your understanding of nine essential areas of professional nursing practice.

cards.title: SECTION 1 · KEY CONCEPTS
cards.body: Accountability, Scope & Ethics

bullets.label: Accountability
bullets.text: Accept responsibility for every action — whether administering medication, documenting care, or educating a patient. Ensure it is done safely and correctly.

bullets.label: Scope of Practice
bullets.text: Understand the limits of your professional role. When a situation exceeds your authority or training, seek guidance from senior staff immediately.

bullets.label: Ethics & Confidentiality
bullets.text: Uphold patient dignity, privacy, and confidentiality at all times. Ethical behaviour is the backbone of professional nursing practice.

cards.title: WHAT IS PROFESSIONAL NURSING?
cards.body: Professional nursing brings together:

bullets.label: More Than a Profession
bullets.text: Nursing is a commitment to safe, compassionate, and ethical care. Patients trust nurses not only for clinical skills, but for their honesty, respect, and professionalism.

bullets.label: Scientific knowledge
bullets.text: — evidence-based clinical practice

bullets.label: Clinical skills
bullets.text: — safe, competent hands-on care

bullets.label: Communication
bullets.text: — clear, empathetic interaction

bullets.label: Compassion
bullets.text: — placing patient wellbeing first

bullets.label: Accountability
bullets.text: Accepting full responsibility for your actions — whether administering medication, documenting care, or educating patients.

bullets.label: Ethics
bullets.text: Upholding honesty, respect, and moral integrity in every patient interaction and clinical decision.

bullets.label: Confidentiality
bullets.text: Protecting sensitive patient information in line with professional and legal obligations at all times.

bullets.label: Scope of Practice
bullets.text: Understanding the limits of your role and seeking guidance when a situation exceeds your training or authority.

cards.title: Accountability in Action
cards.body: Being accountable means owning your decisions — before, during, and after care is delivered.

bullets.label: Administering Medication
bullets.text: You are responsible for the right drug, right dose, right patient, right route, and right time.

bullets.label: Documenting Care
bullets.text: Accurate records protect patients and reflect the standard of care provided.

bullets.label: Patient Education
bullets.text: Ensure information is clearly understood and appropriately tailored to the patient's needs.

cards.title: Knowing Your Scope of Practice
cards.body: Every nurse must recognise the limits of their professional role. When a situation falls outside your training or authority, seeking guidance is not a weakness — it is a professional obligation.

bullets.label: Identify the Situation
bullets.text: Assess whether the task is within your competence

bullets.label: Pause and Reflect
bullets.text: Never proceed if you have doubts about safety or authority

bullets.label: Seek Supervision
bullets.text: Consult a senior nurse or the healthcare team immediately

cards.title: CLINICAL EXAMPLE
cards.body: Priya, a newly graduated nurse, is asked to insert a central venous catheter. She has observed the procedure but has never been trained to perform it independently.

bullets.label: Priya's Story: Accountability in Practice
bullets.text: Priya, a newly graduated nurse, is asked to insert a central venous catheter. She has observed the procedure but has never been trained to perform it independently.

bullets.label: Protects the patient from potential harm
bullets.text: Demonstrates genuine professional accountability

bullets.label: Reflects confidence in recognising one's limits
bullets.text: Builds trust within the healthcare team

cards.callout: Rather than attempting the procedure alone, Priya informs her senior nurse and requests supervision. This decision: Seeking help when needed is a sign of professionalism, not inadequacy.

bullets.label: Knowledge, Ethics & Compassion
bullets.text: Professional nursing is built on all three — none can be compromised.

bullets.label: Total Accountability
bullets.text: You are responsible for every action you perform, document, or delegate.

bullets.label: Practise Within Your Competence
bullets.text: Always work within your scope of practice and escalate when appropriate.

bullets.label: Ask for Help
bullets.text: Never hesitate to seek assistance — patient safety always comes first.

cards.title: Your Foundation Starts Here
cards.body: These principles are the bedrock of every nursing role — in any country, any setting, any speciality. As you progress through the GNPS programme, return to these foundations whenever you face clinical or ethical challenges.

cards.title: Section 2 Overview
cards.body: Patient Safety & Quality Care . Every day, nurses make decisions that protect patients from harm and improve health outcomes.

bullets.label: Patient safety is the
bullets.text: foundation of nursing practice

cards.callout: Even small actions — such as checking a patient's identity or securing bed rails — can prevent serious incidents and save lives. This section aligns directly with NCLEX core competencies in Safe and Effective Care Environment.

cards.title: Learning Outcomes
cards.body: By the end of this section, you will be able to:

bullets.label: Identify Risks
bullets.text: Recognise common patient safety risks in everyday clinical settings.

bullets.label: Apply Strategies
bullets.text: Apply basic risk reduction strategies to protect patients from harm.

bullets.label: Promote Quality
bullets.text: Champion quality care principles in all aspects of daily nursing practice.

cards.title: What Is Patient Safety?
cards.body: . It is a proactive approach — not a reactive one — embedded in every clinical decision a nurse makes. Safe nursing practice requires vigilance, communication, and a commitment to continuous improvement.

bullets.label: Patient safety means
bullets.text: recognising hazards before they cause harm

cards.title: The Four Pillars of Quality Care
cards.body: Quality care is defined by four essential attributes that guide nursing decisions at every level.

bullets.label: Safe
bullets.text: Avoiding harm to patients during the delivery of care.

bullets.label: Effective
bullets.text: Providing evidence-based care that achieves the best outcomes.

bullets.label: Patient-Centred
bullets.text: Respecting individual needs, preferences, and values.

bullets.label: Timely
bullets.text: Reducing delays that may harm patients or waste resources.

cards.title: Clinical Example in Practice
cards.body: This brief, three-second check prevents a potentially life-threatening medication error.

cards.callout: A small habit, practised consistently, is the difference between safe care and a critical incident.

bullets.label: Medication Errors
bullets.text: Wrong patient, wrong dose, wrong drug — all preventable with systematic checks.

bullets.label: Falls & Pressure Injuries
bullets.text: Environmental hazards and mobility limitations increase patient vulnerability.

bullets.label: Infection Risk
bullets.text: Poor hand hygiene and inadequate equipment sterilisation spread preventable infections.

bullets.label: Communication Failures
bullets.text: Incomplete handovers or unclear documentation can lead to missed treatments.

cards.title: Risk Reduction in Practice
cards.body: Identify Hazard Assess Risk

bullets.label: Report & Escalate
bullets.text: Every nurse follows this cycle — consciously or instinctively — in every clinical encounter. Making it a deliberate habit ensures consistent, high-quality safe care delivery.

bullets.label: Speak Up
bullets.text: Every team member has the right — and duty — to raise a safety concern.

bullets.label: Report Hazards
bullets.text: Report incidents and near-misses immediately via your organisation's system.

bullets.label: Collaborate
bullets.text: Safe outcomes rely on open communication across the entire care team.

cards.title: Section 3: Infection Prevention and Control
cards.body: Infection prevention is not optional — it is a core professional responsibility for every nurse, every shift.

bullets.label: Why It Matters
bullets.text: Preventing infection is one of the most effective ways nurses protect both

bullets.label: patients and themselves
bullets.text: . Many healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) are entirely preventable through consistent, evidence-based infection control practices.

cards.title: Learning Outcomes
cards.body: By the end of this section, you should be able to:

bullets.label: Explain Transmission
bullets.text: Describe how infections spread within healthcare settings

bullets.label: Perform Hand Hygiene
bullets.text: Demonstrate correct and effective hand hygiene technique

bullets.label: Use PPE Correctly
bullets.text: Select and apply Personal Protective Equipment appropriately

bullets.label: Apply Standard Precautions
bullets.text: Implement standard precautions consistently with every patient

cards.title: Breaking the Chain of Infection
cards.body: Infection spreads through a predictable chain. Breaking any link stops transmission.

bullets.label: Hand hygiene
bullets.text: — removes pathogens from the hands

bullets.label: Equipment cleaning
bullets.text: — removes contaminated surfaces

cards.callout: Nursing interventions target multiple links simultaneously: PPE — creates a physical barrier Safe waste disposal — eliminates reservoirs Clean environment — reduces pathogen load

bullets.label: Hand Hygiene
bullets.text: The single most effective measure to prevent the spread of infection

bullets.label: Personal Protective Equipment
bullets.text: Gloves, aprons, masks, and eye protection used appropriately

bullets.label: Safe Waste Disposal
bullets.text: Correct segregation and disposal of clinical and sharps waste

bullets.label: Equipment Cleaning
bullets.text: Decontamination of patient equipment between each use
